name: Crowdfunding

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding lets a hardware producer collect payment before manufacturing, so the initial production run does not have to be financed out of the producer's own capital.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can get the money up front for your widget. You don't have to fork out that $10,000 to build a hundred units
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Larry Sears - Hexagram Hardware Holism

claims.claim_text: A reward-based pledge is a purchase order rather than an equity investment: the backer buys a promised unit and acquires no stake in the company and no claim on its future revenue.
claims.quote_verbatim: the misconception is that you're investing in the company. You're not. You're simply placing an order
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Larry Sears - Hexagram Hardware Holism

claims.claim_text: Mail-order and card-payment rules oblige a seller to be able to supply the goods being charged for, a requirement that a pledge for an unbuilt product sits awkwardly against.
claims.quote_verbatim: there are certain laws governing the fact that you have to be able to produce the product
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Larry Sears - Hexagram Hardware Holism

claims.claim_text: A campaign measures demand before inventory is committed: tiered pledge levels return both capital and a quantified reading of how many buyers exist at each price.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can actually gauge interest up front
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Adafruit, Chip heist, Hackerspaces - The Kit Conniption

claims.claim_text: Accepting backer money converts a discretionary project into a fixed obligation, removing the option to abandon or delay the product without consequence.
claims.quote_verbatim: then you are locked in to satisfying people
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Adafruit, Chip heist, Hackerspaces - The Kit Conniption

claims.claim_text: Support and communication load scales linearly with backer count, so a campaign that raises money from a thousand small contributors also creates a thousand ongoing correspondents.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you take a thousand bucks from a thousand people right you will have a thousand people emailing you every week
claims.episode_title: Kismetic Keithley Katowse

claims.claim_text: Funding a project entirely from the founder's own money leaves no external obligation attached to the outcome, which is the trade being made against the speed of raised capital.
claims.quote_verbatim: I spend my own money, do it, and then I don't owe anyone anything
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Callow Cough Coverups

claims.claim_text: Equity crowdfunding proposals under the United States JOBS Act contemplated per-investor caps of around ten thousand dollars and up to a thousand investors, capping a company's raise near a million dollars; the stated concern was that unsophisticated investors could not evaluate technical claims.
claims.quote_verbatim: invest up to like 10,000 bucks into small companies up to a thousand people can do it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Gnomic Gazumping Gobemouche

claims.claim_text: Equity crowdfunding under the JOBS Act remained unimplemented for years after passage, so reward-based pre-sale platforms remained the only practical route for small hardware raises.
claims.quote_verbatim: First off, that still isn't in place, the JOBS Act.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: A producer who already commands an audience can take pre-orders directly from their own site and obtain the same capital and demand signal; the platform's distinctive value is reach for creators with no audience of their own.
claims.quote_verbatim: I could just put it up on my website and take pre-orders
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Mars, Makerbot & Power Outages - Reprobate Replicator Replication

claims.claim_text: Presentation work, particularly the campaign video, is a principal determinant of whether a campaign funds, so it is front-loaded effort rather than a finishing touch.
claims.quote_verbatim: it pays to stand out, like with that video
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - The Ternary Tussle

claims.claim_text: The size of a creator's pre-existing following, measured for example in social-media followers, is among the strongest predictors of whether a campaign reaches its goal.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of the main factors is how many followers do you have on Facebook
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: Because raising capital through a campaign is easy relative to executing a hardware product, funding can be obtained for ideas whose execution path has not been worked out, and the failure surfaces only after the money is committed.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's so easy to try and raise capital these days
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: Platform availability is jurisdictional: Kickstarter was for years restricted to creators in a small number of countries, which forced creators elsewhere onto domestic platforms.
claims.quote_verbatim: Doesn't work in Australia, nope.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Adafruit, Chip heist, Hackerspaces - The Kit Conniption

claims.claim_text: A campaign fronted by an established audience can dispense with production values entirely: a bare pledge page reached its two-and-a-half-thousand-dollar target, covering roughly five hundred boards, within a day of launch.
claims.quote_verbatim: I didn't bother doing a video or any of that crap
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Troubleshooting, PCBs and LEDs - Quaintized Quich Quelling

claims.claim_text: A sudden inflow of many small payments resembles a money-laundering pattern to payment processors and banks, and can trigger compliance review that delays release of the raised funds to the creator.
claims.quote_verbatim: because it looks for some reason that looks like you're a money launderer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Troubleshooting, PCBs and LEDs - Quaintized Quich Quelling

claims.claim_text: A campaign can serve as the launch of a continuing product line rather than a single production event: the Ubertooth One raised about fifty-three thousand dollars against a sixteen-thousand-dollar goal from 441 backers, and ordinary sales after fulfilment exceeded the campaign itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: within a couple months of delivering my units to Kickstarter backers, I had enough additional sales, post-Kickstarter sales, that I was able to quit my day job
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Every increment of money raised is an increment of units owed, so a rising total during a live campaign is a growing manufacturing commitment rather than a growing surplus.
claims.quote_verbatim: I see that number go up and I'm like, oh, wow, that's a big obligation. That's a lot more units.
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Average pledge size on a hardware campaign runs on the order of two hundred and forty dollars, which allows a raise to be estimated as expected backer count multiplied by that figure.
claims.quote_verbatim: the average backing is about $240
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Specialized and/or Open Source Test Gear and Dev Boards - Vacation Videography Vorboten

claims.claim_text: A million dollars raised buys roughly five staff for a year before any manufacturing is paid for, and the sum is revenue against promised goods rather than profit.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's five people if you're not building stuff
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: Funding goals are frequently set below the true cost of the project because an honest figure would not fund, which strands the project part-way through production once the shortfall becomes apparent.
claims.quote_verbatim: They have to set it at $500,000 and then they get painted in a corner when they only make a million and a half and then they run out of money
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Intense Illusion Introduction

claims.claim_text: Even a highly successful hardware campaign ships on the order of ten thousand units or fewer, two to three orders of magnitude below consumer production runs, so the volume never reaches the price breaks and process maturity of mass manufacturing.
claims.quote_verbatim: the production runs that I'm used to is in the hundreds of thousands in toys
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: An interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Absorptive Augmented Actuality

claims.claim_text: A self-hosted campaign can run on payment pre-authorisation rather than immediate capture, deferring collection until shipment; this removes the backer's exposure to a creator who never delivers and substitutes for the platform's trust function.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were able to defer actually collecting the money until shipping
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Non-delivery divides into two distinct causes with different signatures: deliberate fraud, and creators who intend to deliver but have no realistic route to manufacture what they promised.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's a huge difference between a genuine scam from the get go that they just want to steal your money and not produce anything. And ones that are just clueless
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: Kickstarter introduced a rule requiring a working prototype rather than a rendering before a hardware campaign could launch, making the existence of physical hardware a precondition of listing.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to have a real prototype, you can't just put a render on there
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: Prototype-evidence rules are applied unevenly: campaigns with working laboratory hardware have been suspended while campaigns showing less have been allowed to run to completion.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've seen a lot worse projects on Kickstarter that have, you know, gone through that have had less of a prototype than this thing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Amazon Moves In, Dave Says Run

claims.claim_text: Platform commission on funds raised runs in the region of six to eight percent, which must be deducted from the headline total before any manufacturing budget is computed.
claims.quote_verbatim: they get, what, 6%, 7%, 8% or something of the 4 million bucks
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Amazon Moves In, Dave Says Run

claims.claim_text: Indiegogo's flexible-funding option releases funds whether or not the target is met, and its lower barrier to listing means a campaign removed from an all-or-nothing platform can relaunch there within a day.
claims.quote_verbatim: within, like, less than a day, they were on Indiegogo with flexible funding
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Amazon Moves In, Dave Says Run

claims.claim_text: A company with an existing product line and the capital to build regardless is running a pre-order, not a crowdfunding campaign; the campaign form is used for the marketing effect and the order-handling infrastructure.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no real need for crowdfunding here. It's like, pre-order, sure, but this is not crowdfunding
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: We're Sorry! But Apple Ain't! - Remorseless RAM Racketeering

claims.claim_text: After a fraudulent campaign passed its screening, Indiegogo removed the clause from its terms and conditions stating that it vetted every product for fraud, ending the platform's contractual claim to due diligence.
claims.quote_verbatim: actually removed a clause from their terms and conditions
claims.episode_title: We're Sorry! But Apple Ain't! - Remorseless RAM Racketeering

claims.claim_text: A professional investor is expected to perform due diligence before committing funds; a backer on a rewards platform has neither the access nor the standing to do the equivalent, which is the structural asymmetry between the two positions.
claims.quote_verbatim: You should do your due diligence and know what you're buying into
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: B Plus Boards and D Minus Cities - Uneath Urban Ubication

claims.claim_text: Backers' cards are charged only when the campaign reaches its goal, after which the entire sum is available to the creator well before delivery; a year between collection and shipment is within the model's normal operation.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get all the money up front and then you can take a year to actually ship
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: We'll Believe It When We See It - Hiring Hypercatalectic Helpelp

claims.claim_text: Professional and institutional buyers resist the pre-order form, because a tool bought against a purchase order is needed for work now and cannot be justified internally with an indefinite delivery date; a campaign therefore reaches enthusiast buyers far more readily than professional ones.
claims.quote_verbatim: you really want the tool on your desk. You know, you don't really want it to be in a pre-order
claims.speaker: Joe Garrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Joe and Mark Garrison - Subtly Spelling SayLeeAy

claims.claim_text: Once design for manufacture is complete and a hundred test units have been built, scaling to very large volume takes at most about eighteen months, so schedules longer than that indicate the design was not actually finished.
claims.quote_verbatim: that it takes more than 18 months to make very large quantity
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: Schedule failure in hardware campaigns arises from the expectations set at launch rather than from manufacturing itself: promising delivery within a month or three of a large order is not a tight schedule but an impossible one.
claims.quote_verbatim: Problem is when people set backers expectations to be like, oh yeah, it'll be here next month
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: Hardware has no equivalent of a software distribution channel and no recompilation step, so a production release must be correct at the point it is committed, unlike an iterative software launch.
claims.quote_verbatim: There is no recompiling hardware there. It's like, you have to be perfect when you go to production
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: A funded campaign paired with working hardware functions as demand evidence for later investors, converting an unproven plan into a demonstrated willingness of strangers to pay.
claims.quote_verbatim: until you have something to physically show people, you're just another smart person with an ambitious plan
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: Build quantity is set above backer count where post-campaign demand from distributors and direct sales is already known: a campaign with about twelve hundred backers was built as two thousand units, with component cost in the tens of thousands of dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: hey, you know, I got enough money from the campaign. I'll make 2,000 units
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Chris Becomes Self Employed - Quixotic Quitting Quaere

claims.claim_text: A small paid beta ahead of the campaign — around thirty units sold through an existing retail channel — supplies real customer feedback and a price check before the pledge terms are fixed.
claims.quote_verbatim: we did this little beta release on Grand Street
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: Production quantity is chosen at a supplier price break rather than at the exact number owed: about sixteen hundred backers plus a few hundred direct orders were built as a run of twenty-five hundred units.
claims.quote_verbatim: we decided to go with 2,500 units because that, you know, economically made sense
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: The characteristic hardware-campaign failure runs: fewer than a hundred units built, money raised, then the real specification learned from backer feedback, the raised capital consumed by redesign rather than production, and the cash exhausted before manufacturing begins.
claims.quote_verbatim: they run out of cash and they, you know, they finally figure out how to make the thing and they have it designed, but now they need to raise more money to actually go and produce it
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: Reward prices are fixed at launch, before the product's real cost is known, so the price promised to backers can turn out to be below the unit cost eventually achieved.
claims.quote_verbatim: They've promised these, you know, rewards or products at a specific price. And they didn't really have their costs really down
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: Preparation for a first campaign includes backing several projects at minimum pledge and following their updates through to delivery, and asking creators who have run campaigns what they know now that they did not know then.
claims.quote_verbatim: Spend $10, back 10 different projects for a buck
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: Platform staff coach campaigns before and during their run, giving feedback on approach and referring creators to outside expertise the platform does not itself hold.
claims.quote_verbatim: Coaching on, you know, how to run a campaign and giving feedback on their approach
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: A striking low headline price attracts disproportionate attention on crowdfunding platforms, which makes the advertised price a promotional device rather than a costed figure.
claims.quote_verbatim: those are often the most popular ones because like you grab attention with like a, oh my gosh, they couldn't possibly make it that cheap
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Toasted Marshmallow Connectors

claims.claim_text: Where the headline unit price cannot cover cost, the margin is recovered on accessories, add-on boards and shipping charges rather than on the advertised item.
claims.quote_verbatim: You make it up on the accessories
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Shifting Away From DIY - Pedetentious PnP Progress

claims.claim_text: Campaign budgets are commonly built by multiplying bill-of-materials cost by quantity, omitting the non-recurring engineering that dominates a first production run: tooling, firmware development and legal costs.
claims.quote_verbatim: there are tooling costs involved. I mean, there's legal costs involved
claims.speaker: Avidan Ross
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Avidan Ross

claims.claim_text: Half a million dollars is a large campaign total and a small business-building budget; companies have failed after successful raises because the sum raised was never sufficient to reach production.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get 500K for a crowdfunding campaign and a lot of companies have gone bust because they didn't get enough
claims.speaker: Avidan Ross
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Avidan Ross

claims.claim_text: The common failure is not raising too little to start but raising a sum that looks large and falls short of manufacturing cost, which remains high even for production in China.
claims.quote_verbatim: they get a lot of money, but it's not enough
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Use The Protection Circuit

claims.claim_text: Over-subscription is a planning case in its own right: funding far beyond the goal multiplies the work owed at the pledged price without improving the margin on each unit.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's something to plan for, plan for too much success
claims.speaker: Bart Dring
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bart Dring

claims.claim_text: The damaging outcome is moderate over-success rather than extreme success: a raise well beyond expectations but not large enough to fund additional capacity leaves the creator committed to volumes their process cannot absorb.
claims.quote_verbatim: wildly more successful than you thought, but not wildly, wildly successful
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Synergy Bus

claims.claim_text: Scope added after funding — extra features and additional reward perks — is a recurring cause of collapse in crowdfunded projects, because each addition consumes budget and schedule already committed to the base product.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll think that they can do this and this and they can add this and add that and, oh, and this extra perk
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Pull The Trigger

claims.claim_text: Reward tiers can be structured so that earlier delivery costs more rather than less, pricing the first production batch as a premium instead of discounting it to early backers.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you want to be the first batch, then you pay a little bit more
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric VanWyk - Meiotic Mountenance Mooshimeter

claims.claim_text: Full safety and compliance testing is uncommon among crowdfunded products, so its presence is a meaningful discriminator when assessing a campaign.
claims.quote_verbatim: This is full compliance tested, safety tested. I mean, how many crowdfunding campaigns do that?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric VanWyk - Meiotic Mountenance Mooshimeter

claims.claim_text: Selling through a campaign does not remove the safety and electromagnetic-compatibility obligations attached to placing a product on the market, but the route allows products to reach users without that testing having been done.
claims.quote_verbatim: The crowdfunding route seems to be a bit of a loophole when it comes to safety and EMC testing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Miller - Sudden SinoAmerican Synthesis

claims.claim_text: Compliance testing is a scheduled, capitalised step before launch: ten units submitted to a compliance house for regulatory assessment, taking on the order of twelve weeks.
claims.quote_verbatim: there are 10 units currently at the assessment
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Milling About

claims.claim_text: Distributor endorsement badges displayed on live campaigns certify only that the bill of materials can be sourced, and carry no assessment of whether the project can be manufactured or delivered.
claims.quote_verbatim: they just checked that they can source all the parts
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Milling About

claims.claim_text: Crowd Supply is a curated product-launch platform restricted to physical products, of which around ninety percent are open hardware in some form, and it selects projects before working with them rather than accepting all listings.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's very curated, and we help the projects along once we decide to work with them
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: A platform can treat delivery as the start rather than the end of the relationship, buying stock and becoming the creator's first reseller so the product remains purchasable after the campaign closes.
claims.quote_verbatim: We essentially become their first reseller.
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: Where the platform holds the order data it can fulfil pledges directly, issuing order and shipping confirmations and handling returns and customer support, removing the survey-and-collect step that otherwise falls to the creator.
claims.quote_verbatim: almost everyone chooses to have us fulfill their pledges as well because we have all the order information
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: Raises on a curated hardware platform span a few hundred dollars to near a million, with unit prices from fifteen to five thousand dollars; selection turns on an existing community and a genuinely new product, excluding repackaged or drop-shipped goods.
claims.quote_verbatim: What you won't see is, you know, repackaged knockoffs
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: Most creators running a first campaign are deep domain experts in the technology they are building and hold none of the logistics, marketing or sales capability that launching a product also requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't have the expertise of the logistics side of things or the marketing side of things or the sales side
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding is a mechanism for mitigating the risk of building unsold inventory, not a new form of marketing; the marketing work of reaching the right people at the right time is unchanged by the platform.
claims.quote_verbatim: crowdfunding is not new marketing. It's new way. It's a new way to mitigate risk
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: A first production batch is better placed with a manufacturer close enough to visit in person, because problems are certain on a run that has never been made before and remote resolution is slow.
claims.quote_verbatim: for the first batch, it's almost always better to, you know, do it somewhere where you can just walk down the street and see it
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: Kickstarter's published position that it is not a store established that a pledge carries no guarantee of delivery and that non-delivery is a matter between backer and creator; platforms offering fulfilment and curation were founded in response to that gap.
claims.quote_verbatim: Kickstarter is not a store
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding and e-commerce impose different platform requirements, including campaign updates and backer education, so an e-commerce back end has to be substantially rebuilt to serve campaigns.
claims.quote_verbatim: crowdfunding and e-commerce are not the same thing
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: A recurring limited-edition subscription obtains payment ahead of production like a campaign, but spreads volume across successive small batches instead of concentrating it in one spike, allowing production and customer relationships to be built up gradually.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a little bit like a mini crowdfunding thing because you get paid ahead of time, but it scales
claims.speaker: Saar Drimer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Saar Drimer

claims.claim_text: A creator who intends to build the product regardless can set the funding minimum at a nominal figure, in one case one dollar; the stated target then conveys nothing about the capital the project actually requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: I put my minimum funding as $1
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: Post-delivery support scales with units shipped, so a thousand-board campaign implies a thousand potential support cases from users the creator has never met — a deterrent for first-time creators without a support process.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would ship a thousand boards out and then I would get a thousand complaints coming back
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: A campaign platform that also operates as a distributor can carry the product from fulfilment into ongoing stocked distribution, avoiding a separate channel search after delivery.
claims.quote_verbatim: crowd supply also can help you transition into distribution pretty well
claims.speaker: Ryan Cousins
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan Cousins

claims.claim_text: Completion of a campaign is governed by its worst component: a single back-ordered line item held the final shipments of one campaign until roughly four years after funding.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's literally like four years, almost to the date
claims.speaker: Ryan Cousins
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan Cousins

claims.claim_text: A public campaign is an effective lead-generation instrument for a consulting practice, producing more enquiries than a website and business cards; the obligation to deliver is what makes the tactic costly.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want to get a consulting business off the ground, launch a crowdfunding campaign
claims.speaker: Ryan Cousins
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan Cousins

claims.claim_text: The same visibility works in reverse: a campaign that took money and failed to deliver becomes a permanent public record against the team that ran it.
claims.quote_verbatim: It doesn't look that great in your consulting resume
claims.speaker: Ryan Cousins
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan Cousins

claims.claim_text: Fulfilment of a single product can require consolidating parts shipped from several countries — in one instance the instrument from South Korea, the enclosure from China and the probes from Taiwan — each leg arranged and paid for separately.
claims.quote_verbatim: The meter comes from South Korea, the case comes from China, and the probes come from Taiwan
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Year End, 2017

claims.claim_text: Direct purchasers who buy outside the campaign are not served ahead of backers; a single production run means everyone waits on the same schedule regardless of channel.
claims.quote_verbatim: they won't get it any earlier than the Kickstarter people
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Year End, 2017

claims.claim_text: Sustained update cadence with photographic evidence is the accepted obligation during a long delay; in one campaign that ran over a year late, part of the delay came from defective components bought through an online marketplace.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were really good in their updates, actually. They were, you know, posting photos and they got bad parts from AliExpress
claims.episode_title: Bill and Dave's Excellent Equipment

claims.claim_text: A campaign page for a general-purpose tool or platform has to demonstrate finished applications rather than list specifications, because a backer decides on the use they can picture rather than on capability in the abstract.
claims.quote_verbatim: it can't just be like, hey, here are the raw specs
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Bill and Dave's Excellent Equipment

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding can finance a production run for an open design that conventional investors would decline, functioning as a test of whether such a product can be made at an affordable price using industrial processes.
claims.quote_verbatim: Use crowdfunding to go into production and make something that any investor would say, this is not a business model
claims.speaker: Nadya Peek
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Nadya Peek - Gallant Gcode Gerontology

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding created the market for turnkey contract manufacturing aimed at small teams, because it produces funded creators who hold money and a design but no manufacturing capability.
claims.quote_verbatim: no one would have invested in a business like this if it weren't for crowd funding
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: A campaign can reveal a market larger than the creator's own estimate: a book aimed at buyers travelling to Shenzhen sold well beyond the number of people the author calculated could plausibly need it.
claims.quote_verbatim: somehow I managed to sell way more copies than I think there are people going to Shenzhen
claims.speaker: Andrew Huang
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bunnie Huang (2nd)

claims.claim_text: Running a campaign publishes the design intent before the product exists, which exposes it to being copied; that exposure is inherent to raising money from the public rather than an incidental risk.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's the part of the risk you take by publicizing your information
claims.episode_title: Monster Scale Production

claims.claim_text: Campaign pricing commits to figures quoted up to two years ahead of delivery, so currency movement and component price changes over that horizon fall on the creator rather than the backer.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're trying to like forecast out by two years or whatever most quotes crowd supply or crowdfunding campaigns do
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Vapor Phase with Saber Kaygusuz

claims.claim_text: Continuing to supply a product after fulfilment requires an ongoing distribution channel, and campaign-launched products have moved onto mainstream distributor catalogues for their repeat production runs.
claims.quote_verbatim: the last time I had to send it to Mouser rather than sending it to CrowdSupply
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Refrigerators and Robots with Amitabh Shrivastava

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding is one of several routes for bringing cash into a hardware business, and the cash position is what determines whether the business survives an external shock such as a component shortage.
claims.quote_verbatim: All of those are ways of getting cash into your business
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: The Joulescope Upgrade with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: The presentation standard rose over time: a campaign launched in 2012 could fund on a video shot by the creator in a spare bedroom, whereas later campaigns required polished material and a demonstrable track record.
claims.quote_verbatim: it has to be a lot more polished and we kind of have to sell ourselves a lot better
claims.speaker: Ken Burns
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: The threshold model can be applied without a general-purpose platform: a minimum order quantity is set, production proceeds only if it is reached, and the price rises after the initial round to reflect on-demand rather than batch production.
claims.quote_verbatim: we set a minimum t-shirt order, and then if we hit that minimum, then it'll go off
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: Platforms differ in what categories of campaign they admit: Indiegogo accepted charitable fundraising that Kickstarter's rules excluded, and funds raised beyond the goal continued to accrue to the project.
claims.quote_verbatim: which is, like, a Kickstarter. But, they allow charities
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Armstrong, Camenzind & Museums - Outstanding Oneirophoros Obituaries

claims.claim_text: Where a goal is set by an irreducible process cost, such as a semiconductor fabrication run, a published breakdown of how the funds will be spent is the material a prospective backer needs to assess it.
claims.quote_verbatim: Have they got a breakdown of how the money's spent?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Mapping Out Nerdery

claims.claim_text: A campaign supplies backer names and addresses as an exportable order database, which handles the logistics of several thousand simultaneous orders more readily than a creator's own shopping cart.
claims.quote_verbatim: they give it to you as an Excel database
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Alternate Info Sources

claims.claim_text: A time-limited campaign creates a deadline and a reason to buy immediately that a permanent listing in a web shop does not, which is why the same product sells differently through the two channels.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's no sense of urgency
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Alternate Info Sources
